# DESIGN.md — Dre's Island Food Services

archetype: editorial-agency
rationale: Dre's sells taste: its clients describe the platters as "curated canvases of color," and it has ten real photographs of that work, so this caterer earns the direction where the work leads and the explanation follows, carried by bold terracotta panels and very large Inter rather than tropical decoration.
interaction_level: L2

personality: [warm, assured, vivid, precise]

typography:
  display: "Inter"
  body: "Inter"
  scale: 1.333
  notes: >
    One family, used with a point of view through size and tracking rather than a second face.
    Display lines (the hero statement and "We Don't Just Cater Food, We Cater an experience.") are Inter 800 at the very top of the scale, tracked -0.03em, with tight 1.0 leading. These are the type moments, and there is one per screen.
    Section headings are Inter 700 at -0.02em.
    Body is Inter 400 at 18px with 1.6 line height, on a measure of no more than 68ch.
    Eyebrows are Inter 600 at 13px, uppercase, tracked +0.08em, in primary on light grounds and in ground on dark ones.
    The one figure, "80+", is set at display size in Inter 800 with tabular numerals.
    Attributions and captions are 14px, in muted on light grounds, and never smaller.
    No italic display, no script, no second family.

palette:
  primary: "#b4452a"
  secondary: "#fffbf4"
  accent: "#f2a93b"
  ground: "#fffbf4"
  surface: "#f6eadb"
  ink: "#2a1510"
  muted: "#6b4e44"
  border: "#e6d5c2"
  application: >
    Primary terracotta is used confidently across whole panels. At least one full-width terracotta panel carries ground-coloured display type, at about 5.3:1. Primary also carries eyebrows, links and the header's call link on cream.
    The page ground is the brand's own cream. Surface is a toasted step from it, used for the contact band.
    Ink is the terracotta driven down to a near-black brown. Ink also serves as the one dark band (reviews), with ground text on it, answering the brand's dark/moody note.
    Muted cocoa holds about 7.3:1 on ground and about 6.3:1 on surface. On the dark band, secondary text uses surface, not muted.
    Accent mango is reserved for the single primary action, "Plan your event", always with ink text on accent (about 8.7:1). On the ink band, accent may also appear as a thin rule or a figure underline.
    Accent is never used as text on cream (about 1.9:1), and never as text or a button on terracotta (about 2.7:1).
    Every neutral is cooked from the terracotta and the cream, like a spice rub, so nothing on the page is framework grey.

composition:
  whitespace: balanced
  photography: dominant
  card_usage: none
  mobile: >
    Every band becomes a single left-aligned column, with no centred stacks.
    Display type steps down two levels: the hero statement goes from about 5rem to 2.6rem, and the terracotta-panel line goes to about 2.2rem.
    The header collapses to the logo plus a tap-to-call link showing (772) 475-4460, so the phone is always one thumb away.
    Gallery photographs become a horizontal swipe, cropped at the edge, keeping their editorial crops rather than shrinking into a grid.
    The "80+" figure stacks above its attribution.
    The enquiry form goes full width with 48px inputs, and the phone number sits above it, not after it.

pages:
  - slug: flavor-oasis
    title: "Flavor Oasis Tasting Event | Dre's Island Food Services"
    description: "Flavor Oasis, Chef Dre's intimate tasting event at Factory 22 in Wesley Chapel, FL: curated tasting stations, live entertainment and beverages included."
    h1: "Flavor Oasis — The Second Edition"
    intent: "What was Flavor Oasis?"
    takes: [offerings]
    sources: ["https://www.dresislandfoodservices.com/flavor-oasis", "https://www.dresislandfoodservices.com/product/flavor-oasis/44"]

composition: >
  The plates are the pitch. Clients book Dre's because the food arrives looking like an event in itself, so the photographs lead at real scale and the selling copy stays short and plain: Jamaican-rooted catering, drop-off or full service, from Dade City.
  Hold back anything the business has not said. There are no packages, no per-head prices and no service area, so the reviews do the persuading: five named clients who keep returning to presentation, responsiveness and 80+ guests fed.
  The terracotta panel carrying their own line, "We Don't Just Cater Food, We Cater an experience.", is the moment the owner will point at.
  The page ends on one route to book: the phone number and a catering enquiry.

sections:
  - id: hero
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Say what Dre's does and where in one large line, beside the plated food in the hero photograph (1791538675_cra6hy.webp, with 1791538677_b5wvlo.webp as the alternate frame).
      The tagline "Jamaican soul. Five-star service." sits with it.
      The frame also carries the phone number (772) 475-4460 exactly as written and one accent "Plan your event" action that goes to the enquiry. Nothing else goes in the frame.
  - id: story
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Their own heading, "We Don't Just Cater Food, We Cater an experience.", is set as the page's largest type on a full terracotta panel.
      Beneath it, give their story in their voice: authentic island spices, presentation, and front-line service from Chef Dre to the team. Make it plain that both drop-off and full-service orders are offered.
      Add no packages, menus, prices or service details beyond what their copy says.
  - id: gallery
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      This is the "Featured Authentic Dishes and Platters" evidence: all eight gallery photographs, at a size where the garnish, pattern and colour reviewers praise can actually be seen, cropped with intent rather than boxed uniformly.
      "Browse some of our previous creative menu items" may introduce it.
      Never use the logo or favicon as gallery images.
  - id: reviews
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Make the trust case in clients' own words on the ink band. Lead with lines from Camille York Adrien's review on presentation and "service smooth as island sand".
      Give the other four with names and relative dates exactly as written.
      One supporting figure, "80+" guests, is attributed to Jean-Luc Adrien's housewarming.
      Add no aggregate rating, no review count and no star graphics beyond the given ratings.
  - id: offerings
    priority: supporting
    show: "1 of 1, chosen as the only listed item, links to flavor-oasis.html"
    intent: >
      Show that Chef Dre also hosts his own tasting events. Present Flavor Oasis — The Second Edition clearly as past, with "This event has ended".
      Include Sat, Aug 1, 6:30 PM - 9:30 PM EDT, Factory 22, 6027 Wesley Grove Blvd, Wesley Chapel, FL 33544, and the $150.00 ticket price, all given as record, never as something to buy.
      Label the section "Events", never "Menu".
  - id: contact
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Convert a planner. Include a catering enquiry form posting to the Kora forms API with form_type "catering". It collects name, email and message (event date and guest count may be optional fields) and uses lazy-loaded reCAPTCHA v2.
      Beside it, show the phone number (772) 475-4460 exactly as written and the address 15029 14th St, Dade City, FL 33523, USA.
      Show no email address, no map and no opening hours, because none exist.

avoid:
  - A three-column icon row of "Drop-off / Full Service / Events", or any "what we do" icon grid.
  - Agency boilerplate such as "full-service catering solutions" or "elevate your event". Use their own words.
  - Centring everything. Display lines and body stay left-aligned, with deliberate asymmetry.
  - Parallax or scroll effects for their own sake. Reveals are quiet and disabled under reduced motion.
  - Tropical clichés: palm fronds, hibiscus clip-art, sunset gradients, Jamaican-flag stripes as decoration, faux-reggae or brush-script fonts.
  - Any shop, cart, "Order Online" or brunch-box item. Those old store pages are empty.
  - Presenting Flavor Oasis as bookable or upcoming. No "Attend", no "Buy tickets", no sponsorship pitch.
  - Invented catering packages, per-head prices, sample menus, service areas or minimum guest counts.
  - Mango accent as text on cream, or as text or a button on terracotta.
  - An email address, social icons, opening hours or an empty map embed.
  - Payment-method logo strips carried over from the old Square site.
  - Stock chafing dishes, stock chefs or any image not in the supplied list.
  - Labelling the services section "Menu".
